minor_characters.name: Madame Giry
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The long-serving box-keeper who tells managers about Box Five, ferries the ghost’s notes, and undergoes multiple comic interrogations (Ch 005, 008, 015, 017–018).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her functions (Box Five lore, delivery of red-ink notes) can be folded into brief, anonymous backstage gossip and letters without altering the stipend trick, Box Five motif, or the main triangle.

minor_characters.name: Meg Giry
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A ballet girl who launches early ghost gossip and chorus-room scares, then recedes (Ch 002–004).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her lines amplify atmosphere that can be conveyed by unnamed ballet chatter without affecting plot or themes.

minor_characters.name: La Sorelli
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Premier danseuse hosting the farewell gala scenes and serving as a focal point for corps de ballet superstition (Ch 002–004).
minor_characters.reason_removable: She is a one-venue social node whose scenes can be pruned to streamline the opening without touching any later causal beats.

minor_characters.name: Little Jammes and her mother (Ma Jammes)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Comic alarmists in the ballet foyer and early ghost rumors (Ch 002–003).
minor_characters.reason_removable: They add color but do not influence any decision or discovery needed by the main story.

minor_characters.name: Mercier (acting‑manager)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A foil in the managers’ office farces and backstage commotion (Ch 004–005, 008, 015, 018–019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His administrative back‑and‑forth can be compressed into narration about the managers’ fiascos without changing outcomes.

minor_characters.name: Remy (the secretary)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Carries notes and reacts to the office pranks and police inquiries (Ch 005, 008, 015, 018–019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Abridged narration can replace his errands and quips with no loss to plot.

minor_characters.name: Gabriel (chorus‑master)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Anxious staffer invoked in early ghost tales and office scenes (Ch 002, 005).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He contributes only to workplace color, not to the central investigation or love story.

minor_characters.name: M. Mifroid (commissary of police)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Leads a brief official inquiry after Christine’s disappearance and into the managers’ complaints (Ch 015, 019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His procedural scenes duplicate what the Persian, narrator, and managers already establish about events.

minor_characters.name: Lachenel (stud‑groom)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Heads the opera stables and fumes over the theft of the white horse César (Ch 008).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The horse business is a comic cul‑de‑sac that neither advances the kidnapping nor any character arc.

minor_characters.name: Pampin (fireman)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Reports seeing a ‘head of fire’ and faints, fueling rumor in the opening (Ch 002).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His cameo can be replaced by generic crew superstition in a sentence.

minor_characters.name: Mamma Valerius
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Christine’s elderly patroness whom Raoul visits to hear of the ‘Angel of Music’ and Christine’s absence (Ch 009, 011).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her exposition can be condensed into Christine’s own letters and the Persian’s dossier without changing Perros, the Angel myth, or motivations.

minor_characters.name: Darius
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The Persian’s servant who admits the narrator and assists the daroga near the end (Ch 027).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He performs minor ushering that can be done in narration.

minor_characters.name: Carolus Fonta
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The baritone Faust whose presence frames onstage scenes around Carlotta and Christine (Ch 008, 014).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is name‑only context for repertoire and can be anonymized with no effect on Carlotta’s defiance or the chandelier disaster.

minor_characters.name: M. Faure (examining magistrate)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A prologue cameo the author consults about the Chagny case (Ch 001).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The investigative frame remains intact via the narrator and the Persian without this official’s aside.

minor_characters.name: M. Isidore Saack and M. Maniera
minor_characters.appearances_summary: An anecdotal pair in Mme Giry’s comic story about jealousy in Box Five (Ch 005).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Their vignette is pure filler inside a deposition that can be cut wholesale.

subplots.name: The managers’ safety‑pin farce and ‘walk backward’ office comedy
subplots.reason_removable: The extended comic business of notes, safety‑pins, and pantomime can be reduced to a single scene of the stipend vanishing from the ‘magic envelope’ without harming the stipend/Box Five through‑line in the synopsis.

subplots.name: The stolen horse César and stables uproar
subplots.reason_removable: This comic detour about a missing stage horse has no bearing on Christine’s abduction, the managers’ humiliation, or the cellar pursuit.

subplots.name: Formal police inquiry led by Commissary Mifroid
subplots.reason_removable: His procedural thread reiterates events the Persian and narrator already supply and does not alter the rescue attempt or finale.

subplots.name: Debienne & Poligny’s farewell ceremonies and supper ‘ghost’ cameo
subplots.reason_removable: The ex‑managers’ party and the supper apparition are flavoring for the transition of power and can be summarized in a line.

subplots.name: Raoul’s Arctic expedition and naval career prospects
subplots.reason_removable: His polar leave and career plans are tangential to the romance, jealousy, and descent into the Opera’s underworld.

subplots.name: Moncharmin’s Memoirs satire thread
subplots.reason_removable: Frequent first‑person managerial asides can be collapsed into brief narration of their gullibility and loss of control.

subplots.name: Mme Giry’s testimonial circus about Box Five
subplots.reason_removable: Her long self‑vindicating deposition and comic anecdotes (Saack/Maniera) add little beyond what a sentence on Box Five’s ‘private’ status already conveys.

digressions.topic: Chagny genealogy and Raoul’s aristocratic family history in depth
digressions.reason_removable: The multi‑page pedigree and estate details slow the plot and are not needed to understand Raoul’s role in the triangle.

digressions.topic: Gala-night roll‑call of composers and an essay on Parisian masks of gaiety
digressions.reason_removable: The taxonomic listing and social commentary are atmospheric but expendable in a tight narrative.

digressions.topic: Extended Scandinavian/Valerius backstory and Raoul’s naval schooling and expedition logistics
digressions.reason_removable: Beyond Christine’s father/Angel legend (which should be retained), the training‑ship, Arctic mission, and travelogue can be drastically pruned.

digressions.topic: Prologue acknowledgments, letters, and side notes about the Commune corpse and library loans
digressions.reason_removable: These authorial courtesies and side anecdotes do not affect the investigative frame or later action.

digressions.topic: Technical exposition of the mirror‑maze torture‑room mechanics (rollers, heating, mirage physics)
digressions.reason_removable: Abridgment can state that Erik’s mirrored chamber simulates jungle heat and desert mirages without the step‑by‑step engineering lecture.

digressions.topic: Persian’s extended excursus on Erik’s Tonkin reed trick, Yildiz‑Kiosk service, and ‘rosy hours of Mazenderan’ minutiae
digressions.reason_removable: While a brief origin note should remain (fairgrounds prodigy, Mazenderan traps), the long geopolitical and technical anecdotes exceed what the synopsis requires.
